transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-06
Start time: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Emma Rodriguez (GlacierPoint - Head Sec); Liam O'Connor (CTO); Priya Singh (DevOps)

Summary (auto-generated): Security intake focusing on integration points and deployment constraints. Customer leans towards private or dedicated due to keys/residency but open to hosted if KMS and audit concerns are addressed.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick round robin?
[00:06] Emma (GlacierPoint): hi, Emma here, head of security. we run infra on AWS mostly, okta for sso.
[00:10] Liam (CTO): Liam, i lead platform and infra. today i'd like to understand how you handle keys, logs, and what options we have for private hosting.
[00:17] Maya: perfect, and ravi is our solutions engineer, he'll jump into the cryptography and logging bits. ravi?
[00:22] Ravi (Redwood SE): hi all, thanks. real quick, i'll try not to nerd out too much but i'll cover kms integration, rbac and audit trails.
[00:28] Priya (DevOps): quick note, we have a compliance window in q1 so timeline matters.
[00:33] Maya: noted. to get started — do you have SOC2 or ISO artifacts today?
[00:38] Emma: we have SOC2 type II for our product but not for vendor stack — we expect vendors to provide their SOC2. we also have some internal iso27001 controls but not certified.
[00:46] Maya: okay, we can share our SOC2 and the relevant scoping notes, we'll include the control mapping.
[00:50] Liam: what's the usual scope for redwood? do you include hosting and key management in scope?
[00:55] Ravi: our SOC2 covers the hosted control plane and operational processes. for key mgmt, if you're using our hosted KMS we document control boundaries. if you bring your own key in dedicated/private, you keep KMS controls on your side.
[01:06] Emma: so BYOK is possible? we need customer-managed keys for certain patient PII workloads.
[01:11] Ravi: yes — we support customer-managed KMS with both dedicated and private deployments. for hosted, we can integrate customer keys via AWS KMS grant flows or external HSMs, though the exact pattern depends on whether you want us to hold the data at rest SES — uh i mean store — sorry.
[01:24] Maya: there's sometimes a bit of word salad in transcripts, but main point: we can do BYOK for most patterns.
[01:29] Priya: ok, for the SAML side we use Okta with SCIM. we want automated provisioning and SCIM sync, plus attrs for RBAC. how mature is that flow in redwood?
[01:39] Ravi: we have SAML 2.0 and SCIM; teams commonly map Okta groups to RBAC roles. we emit audit logs for auth events and role changes. some older clients saw attribute mapping issues — depends on Okta config — but we usually work through it with a short integration sprint.
[01:52] Emma: audit logs — we need immutable logs for 12 months and ability to export to our SIEM. do you ship logs to external sinks?
[02:00] Ravi: yes, we can stream audit logs to customer S3 buckets, or to syslog/SEIM endpoints via Kinesis/Firehose. retention on our side configurable; for private deployments you control the retention directly. for hosted, we have default retention windows but can negotiate longer retention via enterprise contracts.
[02:18] Liam: latency question — our application needs sub-150ms tail latency for inference in EU region. how does hosted compare to dedicated?
[02:27] Maya: hosted is generally fastest time to value, but dedicated reserved pools are better for predictable p95s. private on-prem will be closest to your network. ravi, any numbers?
[02:36] Ravi: typical hosted p95 is ~200ms for the open models at medium sequence length in us-west; dedicated with pinned GPUs pushes down to ~90-120ms, depends on batch settings. those numbers vary a lot with model and kv cache hit rate — some of our older tests show the kv cache mis-typed on notes as k v cash so watch for that.
[02:54] Priya: that's helpful. our concern is we can't tolerate hosted service where we don't control keys or logs for regulated workloads. any customers run hosted with BYOK and full log export?
[03:04] Ravi: yes a few customers run hosted with customer KMS and outbound log streaming. the tradeoff is complexity of rotation and slight increases in token-neg latency during key handshake but it's manageable.
[03:14] Emma: encryption at rest and in transit — do you use TLS? are client certs an option?
[03:19] Ravi: TLS is standard; mTLS for private deployments is supported. for hosted, we support TLS with certs, and we can add client certs for mutual TLS for specific routes.
[03:28] Maya: can you describe desired success criteria for a pilot?
[03:31] Liam: prove we can do SAML onboarding with group-to-role mapping, verify audit log export to our S3 and SIEM, and test inference latency with a small set of models.
[03:41] Priya: and validate KMS integration with our key alias and rotation.
[03:45] Ravi: good — so pilot includes auth integration, log export, KMS test, and a latency benchmark. we'll propose config for hosted vs dedicated and cost delta.
[03:55] Emma: one more, data retention: we have rules for customer PII to be purged after 90 days unless flagged. does redwood keep prompts or cache?
[04:03] Ravi: our runtime uses KV caching to speed up repeated prompts. by default some prefix caching is stored for a short TTL; we can disable caching per-route or set TTLs to meet your retention. for historic transcripts we can configure purge and provide deletion API. but some models keep request traces for debugging — those are controlled by retention policies.
[04:23] Emma: we need a deletion certification for compliance — basically proof that data was purged. can you provide that?
[04:29] Maya: yes, we produce logs of deletion actions and can provide attestations as part of enterprise onboarding. we'll include the deletion workflow in the security pack.
[04:37] Liam: about network isolation — does redwood provide VPC peering or private link?
[04:42] Ravi: we support VPC endpoints and private link for dedicated and private. hosted has limited VPC peering; we typically use private connectors or proxies. for fully air-gapped on-prem we ship a private package.
[04:56] Priya: okay, onboarding steps? what do you need from us to start the pilot?
[05:01] Maya: we'll need SAML metadata, SCIM config, a KMS key alias or details on your HSM, and a short prompt/requests set for latency tests. also contact for SIEM and s3 bucket for logs.
[05:12] Priya: we can share those — timeline: we can get SAML metadata and KMS alias within a week.
[05:18] Emma: also need to check regulatory boundary — some workloads must stay in eu-west-1. can you pin region?
[05:23] Ravi: yes region pinning is supported for dedicated and private. hosted we have region selections but not strict physical isolation unless we provision dedicated capacity in that region.
[05:34] Liam: cost question — if we run dedicated in eu-west, how do you price? is there a minimum commit?
[05:40] Maya: dedicated is reserved GPU pools, monthly commitment. we'll give a sample quote in the next doc. pilot can be on a temporary reserved pool or on hosted burst capacity.
[05:50] Emma: compliance: do you support SSO session length controls and step-up auth? we might need step-up for sensitive endpoints.
[05:58] Ravi: yes we integrate with Okta session policies; step-up can be enforced through our auth gateway. some fine-grained policies require extra config but it's doable.
[06:08] Maya: anything on retention or DLP that i missed?
[06:11] Emma: DLP hooks — can we plug in a classification hook to intercept prompts before sending to model?
[06:17] Ravi: we have request filters and pre-send webhooks that can run classification; in private deployments you can install your own rule engines inline. hosted we provide webhook hooks to call your classifier prior to inference.
[06:30] Priya: that's key for us. we do a PII scrubber pre-send. want to avoid leakage.
[06:35] Maya: great — we'll include sample webhook config and a PII scrubber example in the package.
[06:41] Liam: can you walk at a high level through the audit trail fields you capture?
[06:45] Ravi: sure — timestamp, request id, route/model, user id if available, role changes, auth events, KMS usage events, and retention/deletion events. we also include hashes of request payloads for verification. note on the transcripts sometimes the word 'hashes' turned into 'hatches' in notes, but it's the hash of request.
[07:06] Emma: hash of payload — are those reversible? we need deterministic hashing so we can correlate across systems but not store raw content.
[07:13] Ravi: we support salted hashes you control the salt for deterministic but not reversible mapping.
[07:19] Priya: what about audit log access controls? who in redwood can see customer logs?
[07:24] Ravi: access is limited to operations engineers with just-in-time access and there is RBAC and session recording. we can provide role lists in the security pack.
[07:33] Maya: okay time check — we're about 8 minutes in — actually the meeting runs longer, but we're roughly at 35%-ish. continuing...
[07:40] Emma: sorry, I was expecting a bit more detail on key rotation — we rotate keys quarterly internally. can we match that?
[07:48] Ravi: for customer-managed keys you control rotation. if we hold envelope keys, we can align rotation with your policy and provide rotation logs. for some flows we use grants rather than full key possession to reduce risk during rotation.
[08:00] Liam: on the legal side, what contract language do you typically include for data residency and key ownership?
[08:06] Maya: we include clauses for customer data ownership, BYOK, and limited access for support. we'll pull a redline sample and share with your legal.
[08:12] Emma: do you provide pen test results or third-party scan artifacts?
[08:16] Ravi: we have pen test summaries and vuln scanning reports; full details are under NDA. SOC2 includes penetration testing scope notes.
[08:24] Priya: for pilot, what's the expected dev effort from our side?
[08:28] Ravi: typically 2-3 engineer-days to wire SAML/SCIM, 1 day to set up log export, 1 day for KMS grant testing, and a day for latency benchmarking. so roughly a week of work with a small team.
[08:40] Liam: that fits our availability. Emma: our compliance team will want a list of controls mapped to our internal policy. can you provide a control mapping?
[08:48] Maya: yes that's included in the security pack. we'll map to SOC2 and provide notes on where private vs hosted differs.
[08:54] Emma: any red flags or known limitations?
[08:57] Ravi: the main limitations are hosted KMS patterns that require an extra handshake which can bump cold-start latency; also some edge cases in SCIM group sync with nested groups — we document these and have standard workarounds.
[09:10] Priya: what about retention of debug/traces — can we opt-out of request tracing?
[09:15] Ravi: yes you can opt-out of request trace collection and still have core audit logs; opt-out reduces ability for us to debug but we can do targeted tracing with your approval.
[09:27] Maya: ok sounds like we have alignment. let's recap next steps.
[09:31] Maya: action items: maya share SOC2 + security pack; ravi draft pilot and runbook; priya share SAML metadata and KMS alias. target dates?
[09:39] Priya: we'll send metadata in 3 business days.
[09:41] Emma: legal will need the sample contracts, can you share the enterprise terms?
[09:45] Maya: yes will include sample contract and dedicated pricing sheet.
[09:48] Liam: schedule the pilot kickoff 2025-11-17 or week of depending on legal, confirm after we review docs.
[09:56] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:59] Emma: thanks.
[10:00] End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions (speaker labels may shift), some technical terms spelled out (e.g., KV cache written as "k v cash"), filler words present. The conversation included detailed asks on SOC2 artifacts, SAML/SCIM steps, KMS BYOK patterns, audit log export, region pinning, and pilot success criteria.
